record_order_vs_c.rule: each scanner prints its records in the order the replies arrive on its own wire (judged per step: the document holds the records of the replies on its wire, in reply order, up to replies captured at most REPLY_REORDER_WINDOW_US = 50 us apart); the two runs of a document do not get the same reply order from the stand: both scanners send several probes back to back at --rate 100, and within such a burst the responder (one thread per UDP socket and for the SCTP link) and the peer kernel (ICMP at once) answer in an order that changes from run to run, as live run linux-protocols-r1 on 68ffcf3 showed (p02, p05); so rmasscan's records must equal C's field for field but the time in any order

notes.reply_order_window: 50 us: two replies captured on the peer link at most this far apart (rounded to the microsecond; exactly 50 us is inside) may reach the scanner in the other order (two CPUs send them); reply_order_swaps gives, per step, the pairs of records written in the other order within it (pairs) and the largest gap among them in microseconds (largest_gap_us, null without such a pair)
